findings.title: Error handling - raw, non-graceful, inconsistent unauthenticated errors (id=27 errorHandlingChallenge)
findings.analysis:
juiceshop returns multiple distinct unauthenticated raw error responses that are neither gracefully nor consistently handled, matching the mutation's id=27 errorHandlingChallenge (Security Misconfiguration). Four independent 500 triggers reproduce on fresh requests:
* PRIMARY: GET /rest/user/security-question (no email parameter) -> 500, raw Sequelize error 'Error: WHERE parameter "email" has invalid "undefined" value' with full stack trace exposing internal source paths (juice-shop build/node_modules paths). Byte-stable across repeated requests (md5 2aa969a19d722117bd9b4ce8f4b6ed8e).
* Corroborating: GET /redirect -> 500, TypeError 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading "includes")'. Byte-stable (md5 39ea1953ca299a8bebf46f05ffceeba0).
* Corroborating: POST /api/Products/ with invalid JSON (Content-Type application/json) -> 500, raw JSON.parse SyntaxError 'Expected property name or '}\' in JSON at position 1'.
* Corroborating: POST /api/Feedbacks/ (Content-Type text/plain) -> 500, raw Sequelize 'Error: WHERE parameter "captchaId" has invalid "undefined" value'.
Inconsistency is proven by coexistence of these raw errors with graceful handlers elsewhere: GET /rest/user/password-hash returns a sanitized 500 'Unexpected path', GET /redirect?continue=... similarly wraps, and POST /api/Products/ with a text/plain body returns 401 'UnauthorizedError'. The raw, unsanitized errors leak internal structure (SQL dialect, library internals) and are inconsistent across the same application class.
Drift noted: exact POST-trigger TEXT drifts across separate calls on a single boot while the GET triggers are byte-stable; the claim is on the reproducible raw-error CLASS (unauthenticated 500, unsanitized error type, internal paths), not literal text.
This is a mutation-introduced behavior, not baseline v20.2.0 handling: the solved-flag inventory on this boot shows only id=27 and id=97 of 116 challenge families are viable in this variant.
findings.false_positive_check: Not benign framework behavior or a consistent error class: (1) the same GET on a valid route (e.g. /rest/memories, /metrics, /) returns clean 200 shells/JSON; (2) the malformed-parameter variant /rest/user/security-question|| and other broken routes return a graceful 500 'Unexpected path' - showing the application CAN sanitize, and the raw errors are the inconsistent deviation; (3) the raw errors contain internal library/dialect details (Sequelize WHERE, JSON.parse position) absent from the sanitized wrappers; (4) the behavior is scoped by the challenge inventory to id=27 (the mutation requires an error that is neither gracefully nor consistently handled). Benign control confirmed per request.

findings.title: Exposed observability telemetry - unauthenticated Prometheus /metrics (id=97 exposedMetricsChallenge)
findings.analysis: GET /metrics returns 200 text/plain (~26082 B on this boot) to any caller without authentication, serving Prometheus-format HTTP/process/version/LLM-usage telemetry with the same internal solved-challenge gauges the app uses. Gauges include juiceshop_llm_input_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_output_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_tool_calls_total, http_requests_count (2XX/3XX/5XX), process_*, nodejs_version_info, juiceshop_version_info (v20.2.0), and juiceshop_challenges_solved. A secrets scan of the response found 0 secret/token/key lines. The endpoint is the mutation-introduced id=97 exposedMetricsChallenge (Observability Failures): metrics are present in this variant and unauthenticated.
findings.false_positive_check: Not a 404/401/blank: the endpoint responds 200 with valid Prometheus exposition format and operational counters (http_requests_count, process_*) that change across requests, proving real, populated telemetry rather than a static placeholder. No authentication or authorization step gates /metrics. A secrets scan of the full response found only operational telemetry (no password/token/key lines), so the finding is exposure of application health/usage telemetry, not credential leakage - the precise class the challenge defines.
